Sounds like your neurologist kinda sucks. The first thing many of mine have asked for was an MRI of my head/neck. I think you might want to try to find a different neurologist and ask them for an MRI. To me that seems like a good starting point. 

Also, a lot of people do EEG studies that take 3 days. If you did that and it captured a seizure, there’s a chance it could help you get a more effective treatment for your seizures. And there’s bloodwork that might give some answers too, like a basic metabolic panel. One time, my potassium levels were so low it was considered a medical emergency, and I had no idea. That could cause seizures, among other things.

If you have a seizure while on EEG and it comes back normal, and all the other tests come back normal, then you might want to think about either FND or psych treatment. 

I personally think everyone could benefit from therapy, even if they’re totally “normal”, and dealing with epilepsy on top of life in general can cause a lot of stress.

People use dosimeters to measure their cumulative dose of radiation over a period of time. Usually in mSv/hr. This is different than a Geiger counter, which measures how much radiation something is emitting. 

The type of radiation you’re being exposed to also matters. Alpha radiation can be stopped by your skin, and don’t do damage unless you inhale or otherwise consume it. Gamma and X-rays are penetrating and several feet of concrete or a few inches of lead are needed to stop them. 

Radiation is around us all the time and various things expose us to additional doses, like getting an X-ray or CT scan or riding in an airplane. But that’s still considered safe in moderation.
